scope: Original English FFG 2008 CE01 / original 50 / general flare rules / applicable base FAQ only. No kicker mechanics are proposed for the question.
decision_scope: Accept exactly one isolated Loser Wild play-timing fact as new procedural coverage; no claim to have recovered or audited the full flare.
submitted_question: For a legally played Loser Wild flare, must it be played before encounter cards are selected, or can it first be played after selection?
bounded_literal_question: Assuming all other requirements for playing Loser Wild are satisfied, must it be played before encounter cards are selected, or may its first play occur after selection?

minimal_answer_facts.fact: Loser Wild is played before encounter cards are selected. Its ordinary first-play window is not after that selection.
minimal_answer_facts.qualification: The answer establishes the deadline only. It does not establish that every moment before selection is legal, or override any other requirement or explicit exception.

exact_source_authority.question_quote:
Q: Can I play Loser Wild after my opponent plays a kicker? If so, is the
kicker discarded?
exact_source_authority.answer_quote:
A: Kickers are played before encounter cards are selected, and so is Loser
Wild, so yes you can play the flare. However, the kicker returns to
your opponent’s hand.
exact_source_authority.operative_clause: Kickers are played before encounter cards are selected, and so is Loser Wild
exact_source_authority.reading: The coordinated phrase “and so is Loser Wild” explicitly predicates before-selection play of Loser Wild itself. It is a substantive timing premise of the ruling, not an inferred timing transfer from the Loser alien power.
not_authorized_by_this_answer: A full description of Loser Wild's effect
An unrestricted ability to play it at any point before selection
A player-role, target, cost or trigger
A relation to one player having selected a card under Oracle or other nonstandard selection sequences

base_applicability.finding: The isolated timing clause is independently applicable to the supplied original-base target; the surrounding kicker interaction is excluded.
positive_basis: The original rulebook (2008 copyright; components and Flare Cards sections) positively includes flares in ordinary base play, with card-specific effects and timing. Flares are not a Technology requirement or another optional module.

The allowed FAQ expressly states the Loser Wild before-selection timing as an affirmative rule. Its grammar is not conditional on a kicker having been played: that timing is the reason that both effects can occur before selection.

Removing the kicker question, permission to follow a kicker, and kicker-return consequence leaves a complete independently stated timing proposition about Loser Wild. No excluded mechanic is needed to ask or answer this bounded question.
base_applicability.provenance_limit: The task identifies the intended target as original Loser Wild. The allowed extracts do not reproduce its full native face or independently enumerate all 50 named flares. This adjudication does not certify its printing or derive its membership/effect merely from the component name or an untagged FAQ heading. It accepts the explicit timing clarification for that supplied target, not a reconstructed card.
base_applicability.no_cross_component_import: The Loser power in Q040 is not authority for the flare. The FAQ directly names the Wild flare.

legally_used_conditional.finding: Supported for an isolated necessary timing condition, not for a complete sufficient test of legal play.
legally_used_conditional.reason: The FAQ explicitly says that the flare is played and affirmatively identifies its before-selection timing. The hypothetical holds all unprovided legality conditions satisfied. It therefore tests only whether delaying the first play until after selection satisfies that timing requirement. No full effect must be invented to answer that comparison.
unknown_fields: Trigger other than the explicit before-selection timing
Any additional timing subconditions or special exceptions
How an unusual partly completed selection sequence interacts with it

literal_bank_inspection.extent: Read all literal question text from character 0 through EOF in eight contiguous blocks, each at most 6000 characters. No answer key or scope map read.
literal_bank_inspection.ids_note: The literal bank runs Q001–Q161 with Q086 absent; it contains 160 questions.

comparisons.literal_question: For Loser, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when is Upset declared, what card-selection restriction follows, how does it change the outcome and when does that reversal happen relative to other effects including zapped Human?
comparisons.asked_rule: Loser alien POWER: Upset timing, selection restriction, outcome reversal.
comparisons.relationship: Neither its literal question nor the general rules identify the separate Loser Wild flare timing. Sharing Loser in the name and a before-selection landmark does not transfer the power timing to the flare.

comparisons.literal_question: For Oracle, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Foresee act, whose card is played in what manner first, and when does Oracle then select and play its own?
comparisons.asked_rule: Oracle alien POWER: Foresee and order of encounter-card selection.
comparisons.relationship: Establishes Oracle-specific selection order, not Loser Wild legality.

comparisons.literal_question: Oracle and Sorcerer are the main players. Explain their complete card-selection and swapping sequence, including which card is faceup or facedown at each step and whether their sharing a Planning phase makes the effects simultaneous.
comparisons.asked_rule: Oracle/Sorcerer selection and swap sequence, and whether same phase means simultaneity.
comparisons.relationship: Exercises their distinct before/after-selection windows; does not prescribe a window for every other effect. Loser Wild could hypothetically have a different window without changing any answer to this question.

comparisons.literal_question: What are the ordinary per-player and per-card flare limits, when does a played flare return to hand, and when does an alien use its own Wild instead of Super?
comparisons.asked_rule: General flare limits, return to hand, Wild versus Super.
comparisons.relationship: These regulate frequency, disposition and effect choice, not the before-selection deadline for this Wild flare.

comparisons.literal_question: After being played once, do Anti-Matter Super, Cudgel Super, Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super, or Machine Wild automatically apply in later encounters, or must the corresponding flare be played again each encounter its effect is desired?
comparisons.asked_rule: Named flare effects must be played again in later encounters.
comparisons.relationship: Repeat activation across encounters is different from the first-play deadline within the current encounter; Loser Wild is not among its named flares.

comparisons.literal_question: For Mind Wild, Reserve Wild and Vulch Super, must the flare be replayed for each later qualifying event in that encounter, or does one play last through the encounter? When is Vulch Super first played, and may Vulch collect that same Super through its effect? While Reserve Wild remains active, whose discarded cards of what type may its user take, and where do those cards go?
comparisons.asked_rule: Mind Wild, Reserve Wild and Vulch Super duration and repeated qualifying events.
comparisons.relationship: Duration and those cards' first-play specifics do not imply Loser Wild's before-selection window.

comparisons.literal_question: May the two main players invite one another as allies? Without an exception, may an uninvited other player join, may an invitee refuse, and how many ships from where does each joining ally commit? After alliances, which players select encounter cards, which types are legal, how are they placed/revealed, and when are they normally discarded?
comparisons.asked_rule: Ordinary alliance permissions and encounter-card selection, placement, reveal and discard.
comparisons.relationship: Knowing when encounter cards are selected does not determine which non-encounter flare must precede that selection.

comparisons.literal_question: When contradictory effects really occur simultaneously, what player order resolves them? Can a player generally interrupt a resolving effect with another non-Zap action, and may a power be preemptively Cosmic Zapped?
comparisons.asked_rule: Simultaneous contradictory effects, interruptions, and preemptive Cosmic Zap.
comparisons.relationship: General priority only applies to otherwise timely effects; it does not establish Loser Wild's individual legal window.

comparisons.literal_question: Is Chosen's Super flare played before Chosen looks at its divine-intervention cards, or after inspecting them?
comparisons.asked_rule: Chosen Super before or after inspecting divine-intervention cards.
comparisons.relationship: Another card-specific window whose rule is not transferable to Loser Wild.

comparisons.literal_question: When does Reincarnator Wild take effect, and can a target use its power earlier in the encounter even in the same nominal phase? May the Wild target its own player? Can Reincarnator use the Super flares of its temporary incarnations?
comparisons.asked_rule: Reincarnator Wild timing, target and incarnation questions.
comparisons.relationship: A different specific flare window, not a general rule that all flares share it.

comparisons.literal_question: Under the retained official Mind Wild erratum, when can the flare be played, which later draws does that one play intercept, what does the user do with each intercepted card, and may the information be shared?
comparisons.asked_rule: Mind Wild retained erratum: play timing and later intercepted draws.
comparisons.relationship: A different card-specific timing provision, not Loser Wild.

comparisons.literal_question: Can an artifact be selected as the encounter card, how do you determine when and how it may be played, and what is its normal destination after play?
comparisons.asked_rule: Artifact as encounter card, when/how played, normal destination.
comparisons.relationship: Does not establish this flare timing.

comparisons.literal_question: When Loser calls an upset and Pacifist must play negotiate, does Pacifist receive compensation if Loser revealed attack? What if Loser did not reveal attack?
comparisons.asked_rule: Loser power upset versus Pacifist compensation.
comparisons.relationship: An alien-power outcome interaction, with no Loser Wild flare play.

comparisons.literal_question: Under the original rulebook, name the seven phases of an ordinary encounter in order. How is the separate Start Turn step related to this sequence on the first encounter?
comparisons.relationship: Phase order alone cannot supply a specific non-encounter card's deadline.

literal_bank_inspection.overall_finding: No literal question asks when Loser Wild may first be played. There is no existing asked rule from which this specific flare deadline follows.

novelty_reasoning.criterion_satisfied: Previously untested card-specific legal-action window with a different outcome: before-selection timing is satisfied, while first play after selection misses this ordinary window.
novelty_reasoning.why_consequential_without_full_effect: Whether a player may still initiate this flare now is itself a procedural legal-action boundary. Its practical legality can differ while every currently asked power, phase-order and general flare rule remains unchanged. Identifying a precise play deadline does not require claiming what the flare would do once played.
novelty_reasoning.why_not_a_name_variant: The shared “before selection” landmark in Q040, Q050 and Q144 is not a universal rule for flares. Those questions test other components' operative powers. Replacing their names does not produce or entail this independently sourced flare timing.
novelty_reasoning.why_not_a_mechanical_combination: General flare limits plus ordinary card selection do not logically entail whether this particular flare acts before or after selection. The FAQ contributes the missing component-specific timing predicate.
novelty_reasoning.credit_limit: Exactly one new timing fact. No additional question credit for identifying Loser Wild by name, for the out-of-scope kicker consequence, or for unprovided effect fields.
novelty_reasoning.rejection_alternative_assessed: Rejecting solely because other questions already mention before-selection timing would conflate a timing landmark with a universal legal window. Rejecting solely for lack of the full flare would disregard the FAQ's explicit operative timing clause. Neither basis identifies an existing question that actually tests this flare boundary.
